claims.text: The single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu coating on Cu is initially FCC.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating contains pre-existing Lomer-Cottrell locks at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a low stacking-fault density at 300 K.
Above 900 K, thermal activation unlocks Lomer-Cottrell locks in FeNiCrCoCu/Cu.
Unlocking of Lomer-Cottrell locks permits rapid stacking-fault accumulation.
Rapid stacking-fault accumulation triggers a localized FCC-to-HCP martensitic transformation.
CoNiCrFeMn nanowires exhibit thermally activated unlocking of Lomer-Cottrell locks at 1000 K.
The localized HCP phase and associated lattice distortion promote amorphization onset.
Unstable, brittle HCP surface patches fracture and generate wear debris.
Fracture and debris generation from HCP patches cause the friction coefficient to increase sharply.
The friction coefficient begins a non-monotonic increase at 900 K.
The friction increase correlates with a sharp rise in the local HCP atom fraction.
The friction increase correlates with a decrease in total dislocation line length.
Decreasing dislocation line length indicates dislocation starvation or transformation-mediated annihilation.
Wear rates increase significantly above 900 K because the HCP-transformed surface layer fractures in a brittle manner.
At 300–600 K, dislocation density decreases slightly while elastic modulus increases.
At 300–600 K, the FeNiCrCoCu/Cu lattice remains stable and FCC-dominated, producing lower friction and greater wear resistance than above 900 K.
Under a 10 m/s loading rate, martensitic transformation dominates over diffusion-controlled oxide formation in FeNiCrCoCu/Cu.
Suppressing FCC-to-HCP transformation should eliminate the friction spike if that transformation is causal.
Persistence of high friction with low HCP counts after transformation suppression would falsify the proposed martensitic mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism place Lomer-Cottrell unlocking before stacking-fault accumulation, whereas the structural_mediator says stacking-fault accumulation leads to unlocking.
